$comment: The catalog of plugins cxagent releases. One entry per directory beside this file.
MACHINE-READABLE ON PURPOSE. The plugin dialog reads this to show what is available and
where to get it, so a future marketplace does not have to parse a README or hardcode a list.
Keep it truthful by hand until something generates it: an entry naming an asset that no
release carries is worse than no entry at all.
`asset` is the file name attached to a GitHub release, not a URL — the version is chosen by
whoever reads this, and pinning a URL here would pin the version too.
`tools` is what the plugin declares in its own sidecar; a mismatch is a bug in one of them.
`requires` is what the USER must install separately, which is the thing a catalog entry can
warn about and an install cannot fix.

plugins.name: csharp-lsp
plugins.description: Go-to-definition, find-references and diagnostics for C#, backed by a language server. Crosses project boundaries: a reference in a test project resolves into the project under test.

requires.description: A C# language server on PATH. csharp-ls is the default and needs no configuration.

settings.server: The language server command. Defaults to csharp-ls.
settings.args: Arguments for it. OmniSharp needs ["-lsp"]; csharp-ls needs none.
